hero.title: Volkswagen CFGB Engine - Replacement Cost, Problems & Compatibility
hero.description: The CFGB is the 170hp high-output variant of the Volkswagen Group’s EA189 2.0-litre TDI common-rail diesel engine, widely fitted to higher-spec trims of the Golf, Passat, and Audi A3 between 2008 and 2013. Reconditioned units are available from £2,200 . The broader EA189 2.0 TDI family generated 1,050 UK replacement requests in 2025 .

costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a CFGB typically takes 8-11 hours at £65/hr (independent specialist rate) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: (All . Fitted = supply price + labour band below.)

The 170hp output of the CFGB means it was often subjected to harder driving cycles than the standard 140hp variants, making turbocharger health and DPF condition the primary drivers of replacement cost. A unit with a documented history of regular DPF regeneration and EGR maintenance will command the higher end of the reconditioned price spectrum. failures.title: Volkswagen CFGB Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: EGR Valve Clogging & DPF Blockage - 2008-2013
items.whatHappens: The EA189 architecture is highly susceptible to carbon buildup in the EGR valve and exhaust gas recirculation pathways. This is frequently exacerbated by the manufacturer's emissions software updates, which altered EGR opening times to reduce NOx output, inadvertently accelerating DPF saturation and restricting exhaust flow.
items.repairVsReplace: Isolated EGR cleaning or forced DPF regeneration can resolve early-stage symptoms. However, severe blockage combined with turbocharger strain or injector coking typically makes a full CFGB engine replacement the more economical long-term solution.

items.title: Turbocharger Failure (Variable Geometry) - 2008-2013
items.whatHappens: Carbon deposits can cause the variable geometry vanes inside the turbocharger to stick, leading to over-boosting or under-boosting conditions. If ignored, this can result in catastrophic turbo failure, sending metallic debris into the intercooler and intake manifold.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbo replacement alone is possible, but if the engine has suffered oil starvation or debris ingestion, a full reconditioned CFGB unit is required to prevent immediate repeat failure.

failures.goodYearsLine: The EA189 family, including the CFGB, is generally robust mechanically, but the post-2009 software updates significantly increased the frequency of emissions-related component failures compared to pre-facelift PD units .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the CFGB
variants.intro: The CFGB engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically located near the oil filter housing or on the upper timing belt cover. It is also clearly listed on your vehicle’s V5C registration document under "Engine Number" and can be definitively verified via a VIN decode.

relatives.description: The older Pumpe Düse units it replaced were mechanically simpler but lacked the refinement and Euro 5 emissions compliance of the CFGB's common-rail system.
- The EA288 successor resolved many of the EA189's EGR and DPF saturation issues while introducing AdBlue for Euro 6 compliance.
- If your vehicle is the 170hp high-output variant rather than the 140hp CFGB, you need the CFFB page, as the turbocharger and ECU mapping differ significantly.
- The Euro 5 equivalent often found in slightly earlier or different market applications; while similar, the CFGB has specific emissions software revisions that affect interchangeability.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement CFGB - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used CFGB is only advisable if it comes with a comprehensive, stamped service history proving regular DPF regenerations and EGR maintenance. Given the known risks of carbon buildup in the 170hp variant, a low-mileage used unit with documented care is the only safe used purchase. Compare used CFGB engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the highly recommended route for the CFGB. A proper reconditioning process will proactively address the EA189's known weaknesses by renewing the EGR valve, cleaning or replacing the DPF, and inspecting the turbocharger, delivering near-new reliability without the premium of a brand-new unit. Compare reconditioned CFGB engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if the CFGB has suffered catastrophic turbo failure that sent debris into the cylinders, or if the vehicle is a high-value Passat or Audi A3 intended for long-term ownership. An upgraded rebuild should include a revised turbocharger and updated EGR components. Compare rebuilt CFGB engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Securing a CFGB through our network guarantees a minimum 12-month warranty, with nationwide delivery and the option for vetted local specialist fitting to ensure the job is done right the first time. Explore supply and fit options
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For typical host vehicles like the Volkswagen Golf Mk6, Passat B6/B7, or Audi A3 8P, current UK market values range from £2,500 to £9,000. A reconditioned CFGB replacement (£2,200-£3,800 supply-only) represents a significant portion of the vehicle's value. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.

items.question: How much does a Volkswagen CFGB engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Volkswagen CFGB engine costs between £2,200 and £3,800 for supply-only, or £2,720 to £4,515 fully fitted by an independent specialist . This pricing reflects the widespread availability of EA189 parts across the UK. Supply-only options allow for independent specialist fitting to manage overall labour costs. → Get CFGB engine replacement quotes

items.question: What is the most common Volkswagen CFGB engine failure?
items.answer: The most documented failure pattern involves EGR valve clogging and DPF blockage, frequently exacerbated by post-Dieselgate emissions software updates. These updates altered EGR opening times to reduce NOx output, inadvertently accelerating carbon buildup and restricting exhaust flow in urban driving conditions. → Compare rebuilt CFGB prices with emissions systems addressed

items.question: Which car models use the Volkswagen CFGB engine?
items.answer: The CFGB engine code is primarily fitted to the Volkswagen Golf Mk6, Passat B6/B7, and Audi A3 8P, serving as the standard 140hp 2.0 TDI common-rail option between 2008 and 2013. It was the volume diesel choice for these models before the EA288 generation arrived. → Check your exact CFGB fitment by registration

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned CFGB engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned CFGB is highly recommended over a used unit due to the known risks of carbon buildup in the EGR and DPF systems. A professionally reconditioned unit ensures these critical emissions components are cleaned or renewed, preventing immediate repeat failures and MOT issues. → View reconditioned CFGB engine options

items.question: How do I know if my car has the CFGB engine?
items.answer: You can confirm the CFGB engine code by checking the vehicle’s V5C registration document under "Engine Number" or by locating the stamped code on the engine block near the oil filter housing. Do not rely solely on the "2.0 TDI" badge, as the CBAB and CFFB share the same external badging but have different internal hardware. → Enter your reg to confirm your CFGB fitment
